A1.justification: Both 21-page PDFs describe the same CoCo study and support comparison of the complete text, equations, figures, and tables. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoCo benchmark results, training-mixture ablations, code-executability measurements, and generated-image examples in Section 4, Tables 1–3, and Figures 6–7.

after.justification: v2 retains the original CoCo experimental results, ablations, code-executability measurements, and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Bagel-based code generation, sandbox rendering, draft-guided refinement, and training losses. No algorithmic component, architecture, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use CoCo-10K and StructVisuals for training and evaluate the same structured-visual and English/Chinese text-rendering coverage through StructT2IBench, OneIG-Bench, and LongText-Bench.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain identical comparator rows. Figure 6 retains the BAGEL, BAGEL Thinking, and DraCo comparisons. The newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same evaluation metrics, sample counts, image-sampling protocols, and training settings, including 16K fine-tuning steps and the learning rate of 2 × 10^-5.

E4.justification: The training-mixture ablation in Table 3, code-executability diagnostic in Figure 7, and adaptive-aspect-ratio analysis in Section 4.4 test the same questions with unchanged evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without seed counts, repeated-training-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All results in Tables 1–3 and Figure 7 match, including CoCo's 73.52% StructT2IBench accuracy, overall text-rendering scores of 0.853 and 0.754, and compilation success counts. The qualitative examples and findings are also retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2) are mathematically identical, including the negative sign in the code-generation loss. No definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same executable-code reasoning framework, CoCo-10K contribution, and claims about structured generation and text-rendering performance.

C2.justification: Sections 4.3–4.4 retain the same interpretations of code supervision, draft-refinement supervision, and programmatic canvas flexibility. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Data-construction tools, frozen components, optimization details, EMA evaluation, and eight-H800 hardware disclosure remain unchanged. The same code URL moves into a labeled front-matter field without changing access information.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds four citations: VideoCoCo, Auto-Rubric as Reward, ProAct-VL, and PerceptionRubrics, listed as references 68–71 in v2. They expand an existing citation group without substantive new discussion or altered novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 hyphenates the title's Code-as-CoT wording, adds Pheng-Ann Heng as an author and corresponding author, revises affiliations, and adds date/contact fields. Citation and bibliography styles change, while the prose and section sequence remain essentially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a document-wide visual redesign with institutional logos, a boxed abstract, purple headings, different typography and page geometry, and restyled captions and tables. The seven figures and three tables retain their scientific content.

improvement.justification: The revision primarily redesigns the presentation, updates front matter, and adds four briefly cited works. Methods, explanations, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. These changes do not establish a meaningful net improvement or deterioration in overall paper quality.
